learning: Pending race. If steering_oscillation falls below about 0.2 with progress near 0.4, the track is the right lever. If oscillation is still above 0.2, reduce kp to about 2.2 next. If max_error stays at 0.062 m with low oscillation, test the sensor row at y = 0.02 m.
notes: Applies the Builder's wheel_track change (0.09 to 0.10 m) with all other geometry and controller values held fixed. This isolates the track effect on oval oscillation, which was 0.272 in iteration 2.
rationale: Iteration 2 (0.09 m track, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, kp 2.5, kd 0.4) gave the best score so far, 111.9, with oval progress 0.44. Its oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.272 from 0.173 at iteration 1 (0.12 m track), above the 0.2 threshold. Line loss stayed at 0 on the oval and s-bend, and the slalom reached 0.9 events. max_error stayed at 0.063 m, so the robot still leaves the track. Turn rate is (vL - vR)/wheel_track, so yaw per unit of command scales roughly as 1/track. Widening 0.09 to 0.10 m cuts yaw gain by about 10%, which is the lever the Builder proposed. I am applying only the track change and keeping kp 2.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.4, the sensor weights and the line-loss rule unchanged. This isolates the track effect, so any change in oscillation or progress comes from wheel_track alone. Expected: oval steering_oscillation falls toward 0.22 or lower, progress holds near 0.4, and line loss stays at 0. I did not reduce kp further in this iteration, because that would confound the test. If oscillation is still above 0.2 after this race, the next step is kp about 2.2. The Builder's 0.06 m off-track floor is unchanged, so max_error near 0.062 m is still expected.
